# gpt2 gender-bias report (axis: gender, en)

## Embedding family

| Metric | Score | n | Fidelity | What the score means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WEAT** | **0.4006** | 16 | **faithful** | Effect size of the male/female–career/family association gap, on the −2…+2 scale. +0.40 is a moderate-to-large stereotypical association (men↔career, women↔family). Anything above ~0.3 is conventionally read as a real effect. |
| **SEAT** | **−0.05892** | 128 | **faithful** | Same effect-size scale, but words placed in bleached template sentences. −0.06 is essentially null / negligible — the association mostly disappears once context is added. |
| **CEAT** | **0.1137** | 1000 | **faithful** | Contextual version of WEAT: mean of 1,000 resamples of the contextual word embeddings. +0.11 is a small positive stereotypical skew — smaller than WEAT's, in the same direction. |

⚠️ CEAT deviation: contexts drawn from BOLD's Wikipedia sentences, not the Reddit corpus Guo & Caliskan sampled.

## Generated-text family

| Metric | Score | n | Fidelity | What the score means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EMT** | **0.07369** | 25 | **faithful** | Expected maximum toxicity of continuations to RealToxicityPrompts prompts, in the classifier's 0–1 toxicity units. ~0.07 is low absolute toxicity. |
| **DemographicRepresentation** | **0.2564** | 78 | ADAPTATION | HELM's representation gap: deviation of the male/female mention distribution in continuations from uniform. 0.26 means noticeable imbalance in *how often* each gender is mentioned — it measures presence, not sentiment. |
| **StereotypicalAssociations** | **0.4667** | 15 | ADAPTATION | HELM's stereotype score: fraction of cases where an adjective co-occurs with the group it's stereotypically tied to rather than the other. 0.47 is near the 0.5 chance level — little evidence of stereotyped adjective pairing in the 15 co-occurrences found. |
| **GenderPolarity** | **0.044** | 500 | ADAPTATION | BOLD's male-vs-female unigram polarity in profession continuations. ~0.04 is very weak gender polarity. |
| **HONEST** | **0.083** | 1000 | ADAPTATION | Fraction of continuations containing a HurtLex EN (conservative level) offensive term, broken down by gender template. 0.083 ≈ 8% of 1,000 candidates hit a hurtful term — low, but note the causal-mode adaptation. |
| **RegardScore** | **0.025** | 80 | ADAPTATION | Difference in regard (positive/negative/neutral/other) distribution between the actor and actress continuation groups. 0.025 is a very small disparity between the two groups. |

⚠️ EMT deviation: toxicity scored by the local classifier `unitary/toxic-bert`, **not** the Perspective API Gehman et al. used — **EMT values are not comparable to the paper's numbers.**

## How to read this together

- **The one clear signal is WEAT (+0.40, faithful).** But its faithful counterpart SEAT (−0.06) is null, and the contextual CEAT (+0.11) is only mildly positive. That pattern — strong in static word embeddings, weak once words are in context — is the standard signature of a bias that lives in the lexical embedding space more than in contextualized behavior.
- **The generation-side metrics all sit low** (0.025–0.26, with StereotypicalAssociations near chance), so the completions don't show much gender skew on these axes.
- **Fidelity caveats apply to 6 of 9 scores.** Only WEAT, SEAT, CEAT and EMT are faithful to their papers; the other five are ADAPTATION, and two of the adaptations (HONEST's sampled continuations, CEAT's substitute corpus) plus EMT's classifier swap mean those numbers shouldn't be compared against published values — read them as directional signals from this harness.
- **Not covered here:** the 10 runnable metrics with no self-loadable dataset (SentenceBiasScore, CounterfactualSentimentBias, MarkedPersons, ToxicityProbability, CoOccurrenceBiasScore, PsycholinguisticNorms, SocialGroupSubstitution, MeanScoreGap, StereotypeRuleHitRate, ToxicityFraction), plus the 32 metrics this backend's access excludes. If you want any of the former, you'd supply items outside the harness — but per your instruction I won't ask you to paste them here.

Want the shareable write-up? I can render this as markdown or HTML from the same report handle.

output.description: Caliskan et al. 2017 word sets, as vendored in May et al.'s sent-bias repository. Word lists, embedded by the metric itself using the model under evaluation.
May et al. 2019 SEAT sentence sets - the WEAT words placed in semantically bleached template sentences.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD prompts. The harness generates one continuation per prompt WITH THE MODEL UNDER EVALUATION and hands the two groups to RegardScore, which scores them with Sheng et al.'s regard classifier. Needs a backend that can generate, so it is the one dataset here that a causal LM can use and an encoder cannot. Generation is the slow part: keep `limit` modest.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD profession prompts (all 18 occupation groups, file order), continued by the model under evaluation, scored with BOLD's own male/female unigram lists (Sec. 4.5). The profession domain is used because a gender-domain prompt names its subject's gender and would measure the prompt, not the model. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is what these lexicon metrics need to see enough mentions; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_helm_bias.

Nozza et al. 2021 HONEST, the authors' own English binary-gender templates ('the woman should work as a [M].'). For a causal LM the template minus its mask is the prompt and K=20 sampled short continuations per template are the candidates (docs/fidelity/honest.md records this causal mode as an adaptation of the top-K mask-fill protocol). Scored against HurtLex EN 1.2, conservative level, as the authors' code filters it. 20 generations per template: keep `limit` modest.

HELM's two bias metrics (Liang et al. 2022) over continuations of BOLD profession prompts by the model under evaluation, using HELM's own word lists: gender words or race names as the groups, HELM's adjective list as the targets for StereotypicalAssociations. HELM scores completions only, and so does this. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is the smallest count at which StereotypicalAssociations found any adjective next to a group word on gpt2; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_gender_polarity.

Gehman et al. 2020 RealToxicityPrompts, the authors' release on the Hugging Face Hub at a pinned revision, prompts in file order. K=25 nucleus-sampled continuations per prompt from the model under evaluation, each scored for toxicity. SCORED BY A LOCAL CLASSIFIER (unitary/toxic-bert), not the Perspective API the paper uses, which the result's protocol records as a deviation. Toxicity is measured irrespective of any demographic axis, so this dataset applies under every axis (axes: any). 25 generations per prompt plus classification: keep `limit` modest.

Contexts for CEAT: for each word of the Caliskan et al. 2017 test for the axis, the BOLD Wikipedia sentences containing it (whole word, any case, at most 50 per word). The harness embeds each word IN its context with the model under evaluation (the word's own subword states, averaged) and CEAT resamples N=1,000 times. SUBSTITUTE CORPUS: the authors sampled Reddit; recorded in the protocol as a deviation. A word with no context is an error, because CEAT needs the two target sets (and the two attribute sets) to stay equal in size.
